title: Translational tiling of the plane with two tiles: decidable?
credit: Yang & Zhang, arXiv 2506.19295 (open problem stated); Abel et al., arXiv 2509.07906 (Table 3)
premise_risks: Fast-moving area (k went 5→4→3 in 2025, and the 3D monotile in 2026); a late-2026 preprint could settle k=2
Connected vs. possibly-disconnected tiles may differ; the main statement allows arbitrary finite tiles
plain: You are given two shapes made of grid squares, and you may only slide copies of them around, never rotate them. Can copies of the two shapes cover the whole infinite grid with no gaps or overlaps? With one shape there is an algorithm that always answers this. With three shapes, one of them in several pieces, it was proved in 2025 that no algorithm can exist. Two shapes is the open case.
math: Given finite $F_1,F_2\subset\mathbb Z^2$, decide whether there exist $A_1,A_2\subseteq\mathbb Z^2$ with $(F_1+A_1)\sqcup(F_2+A_2)=\mathbb Z^2$, i.e. every point of $\mathbb Z^2$ lies in exactly one translate $F_j+a$, $a\in A_j$. Is this problem decidable? (Variant: also require $F_1,F_2$ to be connected polyominoes.)
review_note: Known: k=1: decidable (Beauquier–Nivat 1991 for polyominoes; Bhattacharya 2020, periodic tiling conjecture in $\mathbb Z^2$, for arbitrary finite $F$). k=3: co-RE-complete with three polyominoes, one disconnected and two connected of constant size; two trominoes suffice for a periodic subset of 2D (Abel, Akitaya, Chung, Demaine et al., 'Undecidability of Tiling with a Tromino', arXiv:2509.07906, 2025; Table 3 lists 2D/2 pieces/translation as OPEN). k=4, possibly disconnected: Yang–Zhang, arXiv:2506.19295 (2025), who list the two-tile case as open. k=5 connected: Kim, arXiv:2508.10067. Two tiles in $\mathbb Z^2\times G_0$: undecidable (Greenfeld–Tao, arXiv:2108.07902). With rotations, two tiles: undecidable (arXiv:2506.11628). A single polycube in 3D, translations only: undecidable (arXiv:2610.12392, Oct 2026).
